translations.text: Pelagius: "nor through any men": not from James or John; it was not an apostle [who made him] an apostle [?].
i.e. of the holy assembly.
which is in Galatia.
may it be.
i.e. it is to him that glory is fitting, not to men nor to creatures.

i.e. I marvel at how quickly you have forsaken the yoke of truth and of the Gospel, i.e. it is evident that you were not wise in your counsel; it is quickly that you have forsaken the yoke of the Gospel.
which is not anything.
i.e. there is no other substance on which the Gospel may be set forth but Christ, for it is he who was prefigured in the Law and is proclaimed in the Gospels.
i.e. to bring you from the Gospel into the bondage of the Law.
i.e. they bring the Gospel to strengthen the old, whereas it would be more fitting to bring the figure to strengthen the truth, i.e. the new.

i.e. it is not worth your while to listen to that, i.e. even if an angel of the angels of heaven should preach to you, do not believe him, nor anyone of the apostles, unless it be what we preach to you; for it will not be good for you to go to hear it [?], for its end will be anathema.
i.e. I persuade.
i.e. that I should preach according to the will of men.
Jerome: not grace but conduct; I was not a good man at first.
i.e. over and above that, i.e. I was a leader at that time.
i.e. beyond my contemporaries.
i.e. beyond everyone.
i.e. to defend the Law.
i.e. to preach the Gospel. This is why he says this: because of the false apostles who said that he had been a disciple of apostles.
i.e. to preach that too.
i.e. we heard of one another; we did not see one another.
i.e. we have news: Paul the persecutor is now a preacher of the faith.
i.e. the return was not soon.

i.e. Barnabas was of the Jews, Titus of the Gentiles; those two knew [?]. It was not to learn that I went there [to] the disciples of Jesus, because they were chosen together for the apostolate of the Gentiles.
"I set it before them", i.e. I recounted it to them, to see whether I had gone wrong in anything there, and I had not.
i.e., not in the presence of everyone.

i.e., there are two opinions here: that Titus was circumcised, or that he was not circumcised. And this is what is true: 'but neither was he compelled to be circumcised', for [?] he would have been circumcised, and Titus was not circumcised.
i.e., their authority would not be great with us, even if it were proper; as Peter for a time gave way out of his humility, eating with the Gentiles.
i.e., but that it should have been steadfast with us from the beginning.
i.e., Peter and James and John.
or [?], i.e., teachings, or person.
i.e., his person is not more eminent than the person of the other apostles, though he is foremost in the faith; for God [does not accept] the person, etc., i.e., for God does not regard the person.
i.e., it was entrusted.
i.e., they did not think our fellowship too much. Pelagius: they agreed, i.e., they agreed that we ought to teach in peace and cooperation, or because we signed the letter about the questions.
i.e., fellowship.
i.e., as teachers of the Gentiles.
i.e., that we should take up collections for the people of rest in Jerusalem.
i.e., even if it had not been said to us.
i.e., it was not a lesson that I read with Peter, but it was a rebuke with which I rebuked him for his indulgence and his compliance toward the Jews.
i.e., he rebuked him deliberately.
i.e., it was fitting [?] to take from it praise of holy humility in Peter and of the righteousness of zeal in Paul.
i.e., this is what had been said to him.
i.e., that you should not take meals with the Gentiles.
though their faith was more perfect.
i.e., through his [?].
i.e., to Judaize, i.e., to accept the law of the Jews.
i.e., why then should we drive out the Gentiles in that way, since it is the same faith that justifies us?
i.e., we, believing in Christ.
i.e., though we are in the faith of Christ, we are sinners if we put our trust in works of the law.
i.e., so that I have killed the desire of the flesh, like Christ.
i.e. [?] it is not I who live
i.e. the reason I live is that Christ is in me
i.e. though I live in the flesh, it is faith in Christ that gives me life
i.e. if it is the law that justifies everyone
i.e. in that case the passion of Christ would achieve nothing
mad
i.e. that is pitiful, O Galatians, your folly
a demon
has deceived (you)
i.e. the passion of Christ was preached to you as though it had been seen; or, it was made known to you as though he had been crucified in front of you
i.e. I have a question for you
i.e. how great is your folly
i.e. at the beginning, when you believed
i.e. in vain, i.e. you get no profit from it
i.e. if it is so, you would have greater knowledge
i.e. just as it was faith, not the works of the law, that sanctified Abraham, so it is faith that has sanctified you
i.e. his faith justified him, as in the New Testament
i.e. he relates this to show that it is faith that sanctifies, and not the works of the law
i.e. the blessing that was given to Abraham comes upon those who have faith
i.e. through transgressing the law
that is not the same at all
i.e. they would not be guilty under the law
i.e. we need not be under the yoke of the law now that Christ has come
i.e. sacrificed, i.e. in place of sin and curse, a blessing
i.e. so that what was promised to Abraham may be fulfilled
i.e. it is not a single benefit that the cross of Christ has brought to us
i.e. his teaching is gentle, i.e. what I say below as a comparison of the testament
i.e. even though
i.e. the law came about after the promise
i.e. and yet its non-fulfilment would have been its annulment
i.e. it was promised to Abraham that in your seed all inheritance, etc.
i.e. and yet it is from that that it was given
i.e. this, then, is what is true
i.e. what is the benefit for which it has been given?
i.e. to correct everyone
i.e. thus, and not from the promise, for the law has not been able to bring about justification
i.e. the law has shown the sins of everyone, as in 'there is none that does good'; or 'has shown', or 'has caught'
i.e. through faith in Jesus Christ
i.e. we have been kept shut in for the receiving of faith
i.e. we were not saved; rather, the benefit of the law was only custody and the revealing of sins
i.e. as a guardian is with children, so that they may not go astray [?]
i.e. from faith in Jesus Christ
i.e. through faith in Jesus
i.e. you are united in Christ
i.e. no one is different in Christ; no one has more worth than another
i.e. if you are in the union of the body of Christ, then you are the offspring of Abraham, and it is you who are the heirs of Abraham
i.e. it is correction and direction over each of the two
i.e. under guardians
i.e. under stewards
i.e. until it is time for him to take possession of land
i.e. he is [?]
i.e. under elements (literally 'alphabets'), i.e. under the commands of the law, or under the teachers of the law
i.e. we had not reached [maturity]
i.e. when the heavenly Father judged it to be the right time
i.e. he means sons by adoption, not by nature
i.e. for it is he who knows how to recognize the Father [?]
i.e. rightly
i.e. what drove you to it?

i.e. why then does he say this, since these men had never been under the law of the Old Testament? It is not hard to answer: for to him it is the same thing to come under the yoke of the law and to serve idols.
i.e. elements (literally 'alphabets')
sabbaths
i.e. the kalends
i.e. the three-month seasons, or the Feast of Tabernacles
i.e. in vain, or good for you
i.e. [?] if what I preach should be in vain for me
i.e. I am, i.e. a man; i.e. imitating me will not be hard for you, because I am a man
i.e. so that you may be as I am
i.e. what I suffered while preaching to you, at the hands of your unbelievers; or: even if you did not suffer in body, you nevertheless suffered with me in mind
i.e. that is nobler, then
Where then is your welcome to us, which was once given to us?
i.e. this is how great the welcome was
i.e. even if it were your eyes [that I asked for], you would have given them to me
i.e. because I enjoin the truth on you
i.e. it is not any other fault [?] that you have against me
i.e. they are jealous of you, i.e. the pseudo-apostles, i.e. they envy you, not out of love for you
i.e. not for your good; not as I [am]: 'the zeal of your house' etc.
i.e. only let it be so with you even in my absence
i.e. if it were possible for me
i.e. to rebuke you
i.e. when I am boasting about you
i.e. if that is what you have chosen
i.e. do you not remember this history?
i.e. not according to the will of the flesh, for they had no fleshly desires in this: Abraham a hundred years old, Sarah ninety years old
i.e. a likeness of the law is made with persons and places
learning [?]
i.e. you will have cause for joy
i.e. it is nothing else that he says
i.e. you will not be saved through the cross of Christ if you serve the law
i.e. whoever goes under the law, he must not omit anything; he is bound to fulfil the whole law
i.e. you do not believe in Christ
i.e. according to your opinion
i.e. to your completion
i.e. from the course on which you were
i.e. though anyone should persuade you
i.e. you, in the Lord
i.e. except what I have preached to you
i.e. whoever he may be
i.e. from the course on which you used to be
i.e. punishment, i.e. it will be avenged on him
i.e. if circumcision is anything, Christ's passion is of no profit.
i.e. I desire it, i.e. I would rather have that than their circumcising you.
i.e. do not give up your freedom for servitude.
i.e. let each serve the other.
i.e. if there is ill-will and revenge in each of you towards the other.
i.e. let there be care in this, so that your piety may not end there, i.e. in your sin without repentance.
i.e. this is my counsel.
i.e. take heed of that.
i.e. if you live according to the will of the Spirit.
wantonness
i.e. everyone knows that they are not worthy of fellowship.
i.e. covetousness
i.e. spells
i.e. carousals
i.e. it would be right for charity to come first, without which the other virtues are not counted.
i.e. so that they have no vices or carnal desires.
i.e. if our life is spiritual, let our deeds be spiritual.
i.e. it is shameful [?] while you are teaching him.
i.e. lest you be tempted.
i.e. endure.
i.e. it is well that another's trouble should be like his own trouble.
i.e. that he is something.
i.e. let him test it against his own conscience.

Jerome: at first he commanded the spiritual to instruct the unlearned well, so that one should bear another's burdens; here, on the other hand, he enjoins that the weaker, once instructed, should do good to their teachers.
i.e. whatever each one does, that is what will help him.
i.e. in every thing that was its need.
i.e. eternal punishment of the [?].
i.e. that will be its reward.
i.e. by faith of work, that we should not cease from doing good, so that we may have eternal life, as is said: 'He who shall persevere', etc.
i.e. when it will be time, i.e. on the Day of Judgement.
i.e. of the new [?] or age.
i.e. doing good to everyone.
i.e. see what I have written to you.
i.e. not [the hand] of anyone else.
i.e. it is the will of the flesh that they teach.
i.e. it is for this that they do good: they wish to have the glory of apostles, and they do not endure the persecution for the cross of Christ.
i.e. they themselves do not fulfil even the Law.
i.e. they desire your circumcision.
i.e. so that the name of apostles may be given to them through preaching circumcision to you.
i.e. I am not like them.
i.e. as a dead man is to the burial of a dead man, so is each of the two to the other: I and the world.
i.e. may there be peace for them with God and with men, i.e. upon those who fulfil the will of God.
i.e. the saints, who see God and who fulfil the will of God.
i.e. henceforth, i.e. though you have done so until now.
i.e. do not provoke me to take vengeance on you.
[?], i.e. the torments of scourgings.
i.e. the insignia of apostleship, i.e. so that I can [inflict] punishment and correction on anyone.
